parsed.explanation: Nepal has no criminalization of gender nonconformity or same-sex conduct and recognized a third gender category ('other'/O) following a landmark 2007 Supreme Court ruling, with constitutional protections against discrimination based on gender identity. Foreign visitors generally encounter functioning border procedures with standard passport recognition (including non-binary markers). Anti-trans violence against foreigners is exceptionally rare, and general cultural attitudes lean toward tolerance or social curiosity/friction rather than ideological hostility. However, legal protections are imperfectly implemented in administrative and custody settings, where birth-sex placement remains standard practice. Facilities lack universal formal gender-neutral accommodations, and local police harassment of visible trans women (primarily local sex workers) occasionally occurs, posing minor incidental risk if outed.
